name: Familial Intestinal Malrotation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Intestinal Malrotation

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of abnormal midgut rotation on upper gastrointestinal contrast study
Positive family history of intestinal malrotation or related congenital anomalies
Symptoms consistent with intestinal obstruction or volvulus such as bilious vomiting or abdominal distension

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiological evidence of abnormal midgut rotation plus either positive family history or clinical presentation consistent with malrotation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not routinely available.

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers in volvulus or ischemia
imaging: Upper gastrointestinal series showing abnormal position of duodenojejunal junction
Abdominal ultrasound with abnormal SMA/SMV relationship
CT scan demonstrating malrotation and volvulus
genetic: Familial clustering suggests possible autosomal dominant inheritance
No specific gene identified; genetic testing currently limited
other: Intraoperative findings of narrow mesenteric base and abnormal bowel fixation

distinguishingFeatures: Congenital absence or closure of intestinal lumen

redFlags: Signs of bowel ischemia (severe abdominal pain, metabolic acidosis)
Rapid abdominal distension with signs of shock
references: Stringer MD. Intestinal malrotation: a review. Pediatr Surg Int. 2005;21(1):1-9.
Durkin ET, Lund DP, Shaaban AF, Schurr MJ, Weber SM. Age-related differences in diagnosis and morbidity of intestinal malrotation. J Am Coll Surg. 2008;206(4):658-63.
